subject: Discount/credit request for delayed streaming API delivery
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@acmeenterprises.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Delgado <tom.delgado@acmeenterprises.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Gap: streaming API availability and billing impact

Connor —

Quick note from the Acme side: our engineering team had planned to switch our real-time features to Redwood streaming in early June. The streaming endpoints are still marked as 'beta / coming soon' in your roadmap, and that left us with a partial DIY solution hauling cost and latency overhead. We're seeing a material impact on our infra spend and some missed SLAs with our customers.

We appreciate the roadmap visibility you shared earlier, but given the delivery delay we need to discuss commercial remediation: a billing credit or discount to offset the extra infra spend we absorbed. Can you share what options Redwood can offer while streaming is not available? We'd like a clear proposal this week so we can close out our Q2 vendor review.

Thanks —
Sara
Sara Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Enterprises
Attachments: (none)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@acmeenterprises.com>
Cc: Tom Delgado <tom.delgado@acmeenterprises.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gap: streaming API availability and billing impact

Sara —

Thanks for raising this and sorry for the friction. I copied Product and Finance so we can give a concrete proposal. Short answer: we want to make this right and I expect we can offer a one-time credit or a short-term bill discount tied to the streaming delivery date.

To be explicit about Acme's ask: you want compensation that meaningfully covers the added infra/engineering cost you incurred between the date you expected streaming and now. If you can share an estimate of incremental spend for May–June (ballpark is fine) I can use that to size the proposal.

Internal ask to Rishi / Marissa / Laura / Neha: can you weigh in on acceptable precedent here? Is Redwood OK with a time-boxed percent credit (e.g., 15–25% for N months) vs a capped one-time credit? Need guidance on approval path (who signs off for >$10k).

Proposed next step: I’ll tell Acme we’ll respond with a formal credit memo by EOD Thursday (7/2) pending internal sign-off.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415-555-0172
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gap: streaming API availability and billing impact

Connor —

Thanks for flagging. A few norms from GTM/renewals:
- We typically offer a short-term percentage credit when a product gap causes measurable customer impact, rather than an uncapped one-time refund. Keeps precedent manageable.
- For enterprise customers on multi-year deals, Sales can escalate credits up to $15k; anything above requires RevOps/Finance sign-off.

Recommendation (fast path): offer Acme a 20% credit on Redwood invoice line-items impacted for three months (July–Sep), capped at $18,000. That should be large enough to signal goodwill and keep them through their go-live.

If Product confirms streaming ship window is <8 weeks, Finance may accept a slightly lower cap (e.g., $12k). If Product says longer, we should consider one-time higher cap.

Connor: I can green-light up to $15k from Sales budget; please route >$15k to Laura. Marissa: can you confirm ETA and whether that ETA is firm enough to justify a 3-month timebox?

- Rishi

On Tue, Jun 30, 2026 at 10:05 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sara —
>
> Thanks for raising this and sorry for the friction. I copied Product and Finance so we can give a concrete proposal...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gap: streaming API availability and billing impact

Folks —

Quick product context: Streaming v2 (public streaming endpoints + SDK) was delayed due to an encoder optimization that introduced a regression in edge latency. We have the patch in code review; current target for customer rollout is week of 2026-08-10 (internal release 2026-08-03). I can confirm the ETA above barring regressions in the next two sprints.

Given that ETA, I support offering a time-boxed credit to Acme while streaming is not available. My preference: 3 monthly credits tied to impacted usage (not total spend), capped at $12,000. That matches Product's confidence window and keeps the total exposure predictable. Please attach the roadmap excerpt (prod-roadmap-streaming-v2.pdf) when sharing with the customer.

If Finance pushes back on the cap, Neha / Laura please advise on approval steps.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachments: prod-roadmap-streaming-v2.pdf
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@acmeenterprises.com>, Tom Delgado <tom.delgado@acmeenterprises.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gap: streaming API availability and billing impact

Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the patience while we assessed options internally. We want to make this right. Here is the formal remediation we can offer: 

Option A (preferred): 3 monthly credits (July–September) applied to impacted usage lines where streaming would have reduced your infra spend. The credit will be 20% of those impacted Redwood charges each month, capped at $12,000 total.

Option B (one-time): single one-time credit of $12,000 applied to your next invoice.

Product has confirmed streaming v2 targeted customer rollout week of 2026-08-10. The credit is intended as goodwill while the feature ships. To accept, please sign the attached Credit Memo (credit-memo-draft.docx) and we'll route the DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder. Once we have the signed memo I'll issue the credit and confirm invoice adjustments.

If you'd prefer a different structure (e.g., percentage for 2 months + capped refund), let me know and I can route for quick approval.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0172
Attachments: credit-memo-draft.docx
